Describe how well columns work as a key

Source: R/describe_key.R
describe_key.Rd

A key should identify each row. When it does not, the next question is what the duplicates are: exact copies of a row, which can simply be dropped, or rows that disagree, which need a rule. describe_key() counts the duplicated keys and how many copies each has, separates exact copies from conflicts, and names the columns the conflicting copies disagree in. It judges nothing; require a key with ensure_unique().

Usage

describe_key(data, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database tables in checkpoints.

...

Key columns (tidy-select). If omitted, all columns are used, which counts fully duplicated rows.

Value

An object of class inshape_key, printed as a summary. It is a list with key (the column names), the counts n_rows, n_keys (distinct keys), n_dup_keys, n_dup_rows (rows sharing a key) and n_exact (duplicated keys whose copies are identical in every column), and three tibbles: copies (copies, keys), conflicts (column, keys: the duplicated keys whose copies differ in that column, most first) and missing (column, rows).

Details

Two copies disagree in a column when their values differ there; a missing value and a present one differ, two missing values do not. Key columns with missing values are counted, since a missing value in a key is usually an error of its own, even when the key is unique.

See also

ensure_unique() to require a unique key and see the rows, describe_panel() for unit-periods.

Examples

firms <- data.frame(
  cvr      = c("1", "1", "2", "2", "3"),
  year     = c(2024, 2024, 2024, 2024, 2024),
  industry = c("A", "A", "B", "C", "A"),
  income   = c(10, 10, 5, 5, 7)
)
# cvr 1 is an exact copy; cvr 2 disagrees on the industry
describe_key(firms, cvr, year)
#> ── Key: cvr, year ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 5 rows, 3 distinct keys
#> 
#> ⚠ Duplicated keys: 2 (4 rows, 2 extra rows)
#> ⚠ Copies differ in: industry (1)
#> • Exact copies, identical in every column: 1 of 2 keys
#> • Copies per duplicated key: 2 (2)
